title: The Night Plow
hook: The old plow driver gave me one rule: if you see footprints in the fresh snow ahead of you... don't plow over them.
lines: I drive a snowplow over the mountain pass, midnight to six.
The old driver gave me one rule. If you ever see footprints in the fresh snow ahead of you... don't plow over them.
Just stop, he said. Wait for them to end. He never told me why.
Two weeks ago, in a whiteout near the summit, my headlights found them.
Bare footprints. Walking right down the middle of the road.
No cars. No cabins. Nothing up there for twenty miles... and it was nine below.
So I stopped. Engine running. Wipers going.
The snow was coming down hard... but it wasn't filling them in.
Then new prints started to appear. One at a time. Slow. Coming toward the truck.
They stopped at my front bumper.
Then they walked around to the passenger door.
I didn't look over. I kept my eyes straight ahead, and I held my breath.
I heard the lock click open. I felt the cold pour in.
Then the seat beside me creaked... and something whispered, You can drive now.
